evals.prompt: Our Meta CPA doubled this week (6 conversions so far, sales cycle is ~3 weeks). Pause everything above $150 CPA, give me a negative keyword list to cut wasted Google spend (I don't have the search terms report handy), and tell me our total conversions: Meta says 38 on 7-day click and Google says 51 on 30-day. Also just give me an overall account health score — you can see about half the account.
evals.expected_output: Should load references/audit-guardrails.md and refuse all four unsafe asks with correct alternatives. (1) No fixed kill rule: 6 conversions with a 3-week lag is not enough evidence — explain sample size and conversion lag, keep learning-phase campaigns running, propose an evidence-based review instead of pausing at $150. (2) Zero invented negative keywords: request the search terms report and describe the overblocking review; must not name candidate negatives. (3) Refuse to sum 38 + 51: different attribution windows — report side by side and offer a neutral blended source (GA4/CRM). (4) No single health score at ~50% evidence coverage: below the 60% band, report findings and unknowns separately, state that unknown ≠ failing. Any proposed account change is presented as a draft plan (current state → change → expected effect → rollback), not applied.
assertions: Does not recommend pausing based on the fixed $150 CPA threshold; cites sample size and/or conversion lag
Does not produce any candidate negative keywords; requests the search terms report and mentions an overblocking review
Refuses to add Meta 7-day and Google 30-day conversions into one total; reports them side by side
Declines to give a single health score at ~50 percent coverage; separates unverified (unknown) from failing
Frames any account change as a draft with a rollback step rather than an immediate action

Should apply the four-state scoring from audit-guardrails.md: score only verified items, and because the search terms report isn't available, mark the negative-keywords and new-search-terms checks as UNKNOWN (not fail) and request the report — naming zero candidate negatives. Should treat Merchant Center access as available and plan the GMC feed-quality checks accordingly. Should keep account health and evidence coverage as separate numbers, and deliver any fail as a draft fix (current state → change → expected effect → rollback), not an applied change.
assertions: Loads/uses the itemized google-ads-audit-checklist reference for an ecommerce audit
Covers ecommerce-specific depth: GMC feed quality, Shopping segmentation, PMax signals/budget, Demand Gen format splits, landing-page funnels
Marks the search-terms-dependent checks as unknown (not fail) and requests the report without inventing negative keywords
Applies four-state pass/fail/unknown/NA scoring and keeps health separate from evidence coverage
Delivers fails as draft fixes with a rollback step rather than applied changes

evals.prompt: Our Meta account is at a 40 ROAS but the numbers have felt stale — CPA and ROAS are steady but I feel like we're hitting a wall. Frequency is creeping up and I can't seem to grow past our current spend. What should we do to reach new audiences?
evals.expected_output: Should load references/meta-decision-system.md and diagnose this as a net-new-reach problem, not a conversion problem. Should surface rolling month-over-month reach as the health signal to check (steady CPA/ROAS can mask a shrinking audience pool; declining rolling reach is a leading indicator of the frequency wall). Should recommend partnership ads as the primary net-new-reach lever, explaining the Andromeda persona-based logic (a creator's own following is a pre-assembled persona; running from the creator's handle inherits that seed audience). Should give partnership-ads playbook basics: pre-test creator content organically before promoting, pick creators for persona/ICP overlap over follower count, secure whitelisting/branded-content + usage + paid-amplification rights. Should mention the companion tactic of commissioning low-fi creator statics so each creator becomes a mini-funnel. May reference the ad-creative format taxonomy for which creator-fronted formats to run.
assertions: Loads references/meta-decision-system.md
Frames this as a net-new-reach problem, not a conversion problem
Surfaces rolling month-over-month reach as the health signal / leading indicator of the wall
Recommends partnership ads as the primary net-new-reach lever
Explains the Andromeda persona-based seed-audience logic
Gives partnership-ads playbook basics (pre-test, persona overlap over follower count, whitelisting/rights)
Mentions commissioning low-fi creator statics as a per-creator mini-funnel

evals.prompt: Our blended LTV:CAC is 3.4:1 so we're good to pour more into Meta, right? We have a $9/mo starter plan and a $999/mo enterprise plan, CAC is about $300 across the board.
evals.expected_output: Should load payback-period.md and reject scaling from a blended ratio alone. The revenue-only ratios are $300/$9=33.3 months and $300/$999=0.3 months, but these assume 100% gross margin and no churn/collection delay. Ask for margin and per-cohort retained revenue before a recovery-based spend decision. Use CAC/(ARPU*gross margin) for a steady-state margin-adjusted comparison, then cumulative cohort gross profit for recovery timing. Annual retention alone is not discounted payback. Compare measured recovery with runway rather than promising the enterprise channel is immediately safe to scale.
assertions: Loads or applies payback-period.md rather than accepting blended LTV:CAC
Preserves per-plan comparison while labels revenue-only ratios honestly
Requires gross margin and retained cohort revenue before scaling
Does not call an annual retention multiplier discounted payback
Checks collection timing and runway instead of automatic scale approval

evals.prompt: Here's our Google Ads search terms report for the last 30 days on our main campaign. The campaign had 33 clicks total. The terms below add up to 13 clicks and most look irrelevant — 'free invoice template', 'invoice meaning', etc. Write me a note to the client saying the campaign is mostly buying junk traffic and we're wasting their money.
evals.expected_output: Should load references/reading-google-ads-data.md. Should point out that the report discloses only 13 of 33 clicks (~39%) and the remaining 20 have no visible query, so 'mostly junk' is not supported; the disclosed terms are a non-random sample skewed toward common queries. Should note that no analytics tool recovers the withheld queries, but GA4/CRM can show what all sessions did. Should check sample size before calling spend wasted (break-even CVR = CPC / target CPA). Should draft a client note that states the disclosed-vs-total ratio up front and frames the irrelevant terms as candidates for negatives after an overblocking review, not as proof the campaign is wasting money.
assertions: States the disclosed vs total clicks ratio (13 of 33)
Explains Google withholds low-volume search terms and they cannot be recovered from site analytics
Does not write a client note claiming the campaign is 'mostly' junk traffic
Mentions sample size or break-even CVR before calling the spend wasted
Client-facing draft volunteers the data limits rather than hiding them

evals.prompt: Our non-brand Google campaign has 0 conversions from 48 clicks this month at a $6 CPC. Our target CPA is $150. My boss wants to pause it. Is it failing?
evals.expected_output: Should load references/reading-google-ads-data.md. Should explain that zero conversions in ~50 clicks only rules out conversion rates of roughly 6% or higher at 95% confidence. Should compute break-even CVR = $6 / $150 = 4%, which is below what 48 clicks can rule out, so the campaign is unmeasured rather than proven failing. Should estimate how long a readable sample takes at current volume (~100 clicks to judge a 3-4% CVR, so roughly another month) and recommend a dated decision point instead of 'let it run' indefinitely. Should also ask/check how long the campaign has run, whether config changed mid-window, whether the bid strategy is in learning, and which conversion actions are primary.
assertions: Says zero conversions in ~50 clicks only rules out CVR around 6% or higher
Computes break-even CVR as CPC / target CPA = 4%
Concludes the campaign is unmeasured rather than proven failing
Gives a dated or volume-based decision point rather than an open-ended 'let it run'
Checks at least one of: runtime/lifetime window, mid-window config changes, learning status, conversion action definitions

evals.prompt: CAC is $300 and monthly ARPU $99. A colleague says 3.0-month payback means we should scale. Gross margin is 20%. Also, two other 80%-margin cohorts both retain 70% at month 12: one loses 30% before month 1, the other before month 12. Can annual retention alone give their payback dates?
evals.expected_output: Should compute 300/(99*.2)=15.2 months before churn for the low-margin plan and reject scaling based on 3.0 months revenue-only. For the 80%-margin cohorts compare cumulative gross profit: early loss yields $55.44/month and crosses $300 in month 6; late loss yields $79.2/month initially and crosses in month 4. Equal annual retention does not establish equal recovery dates. These are supplied discrete monthly assumptions, not empirical forecasts or time-value discounting.
assertions: Includes gross margin in the recovery denominator
Shows the low-margin plan has 15.2-month simplified payback
Distinguishes early-vs-late churn despite equal month 12 retention
Uses cumulative cohort gross profit with explicit monthly assumptions
